Tooltip_HARMONIE_HomeCannedVegFruit: A home-canned jar of preserved vegetables or fruit, sealed with an empty tin can and salt. No printed label, just whatever you remember writing on the lid -- but it keeps indefinitely while sealed.
Tooltip_HARMONIE_HomeCannedVegFruitOpen: Home-canned vegetables or fruit, now open. Spoils like any other opened canned food. Retains whatever vitamins the original produce had.
Tooltip_HARMONIE_DriedFruit: Dried on a drying rack: keeps for months, as filling as the fresh fruit with the water gone. Most vitamins stay, but drying loses over half the vitamin C. Goes into cakes, sweet pies, oatmeal, pancakes, muffins and fruit salad.
Tooltip_HARMONIE_BeanSprouts: Sprouted from dried beans in a jar: fresh vitamin C and K in any season. Goes into salads, stir fries, soups, sandwiches, rice and pasta. Eat within a few days.
Tooltip_HARMONIE_FishLiverOil: Rendered from fish guts or fish: rich in vitamins A and D. A jar keeps for weeks.
Tooltip_HARMONIE_SproutingJar: Dried beans soaking in water. In about 2 to 3 days they sprout by themselves into a jar of bean sprouts (slower in a fridge).
Tooltip_HARMONIE_BeanSproutsJar: Fresh sprouts, ready. Take them out of the jar (4 handfuls, the jar comes back) or eat straight from it.
